title: A quiet ci-job step does not trip the stall watch and strand its jobs
why: Batch runner, batch 37 (#900), Oct 31 (via coordinator): a ci-job step quiet for over 300 s trips the stall watch; the stall exit leaves its jobs running, and the guard then refuses to stop them. Cost real time today.
note: Fix the cause: either ci-job prints a heartbeat while a step runs, or the stall watch exits by stopping the processes it started, so nothing is stranded. The guard's refusal to kill a job the session itself started is then not met. Done check: a test with a step quiet past the stall limit ends with no process left running, red on main and green on the fix. Needs no answer. Files: bin/ci-job, hooks/stall_watch.py.
